items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: Let me see, it was Lips Page, Walter Page, Buster Smith, Dan Miner... I think so. But I know I named the ones that I remember was there. Just like I say, Page and Buster Smith, Lips Page, Dan Miner

ctx.x: But not everybody has that kind of mind, where you go and buy books or get books.

When we made this Kansas City story, he bought a -- brought a trunk of blues music. And some of that stuff, you never realize it needs to be on the market. I hear from him all the time. We went over some of it, and boy, -- he's the guy that really did The One O'Clock Jump. The score was there, he brought the music, played it off this -- and the other way the other parts got added in was, like, it didn't have nothing to do with the trombones because everybody was hitting the same way and always could come up with…
but that's how he did it. Then they started calling me Circus Boy. There's old Circus.
